title: Porque vs Por Qué: Porque, Por qué, Porqué and Por que
seo_title: Porque vs Por Qué: Porque, Por qué, Porqué and Por que
meta_description: Porque vs por qué: the four Spanish forms explained, why vs because, el porqué, por que, with simple rules, examples, common mistakes and a quick quiz.
excerpt: Four spellings, four meanings: a simple guide to why and because in Spanish.
body_html:
Porque vs por qué is a spelling question that even native speakers get wrong. Spanish has four forms: por qué (why), porque (because), el porqué (the reason) and the rare por que. They sound almost identical, so the difference lives in writing. The good news: two of them cover 95% of real use, and the rule for those two is very simple.

Quick answer
  • ¿Por qué? = why (questions, direct or indirect).
  • Porque = because (answers, reasons).
  • El porqué = the reason (a noun, with an article).
  • Por que = for which / that (rare, preposition + relative or conjunction).
{{toc}}

Porque vs por qué: the four forms

FormMeaningExample
por quéwhy¿Por qué lloras? Why are you crying?
porquebecausePorque estoy triste. Because I’m sad.
porquéthe reason (noun)No entiendo el porqué. I don’t understand the reason.
por quefor which; (that)La razón por que lo hizo… The reason for which he did it…

The RAE’s Diccionario panhispánico de dudas sets out all four forms with examples.

Por qué: asking why

Two words, accent on qué. Use it in direct and indirect questions:

  • ¿Por qué no viniste? Why didn’t you come?
  • No sé por qué está enfadado. I don’t know why he’s angry.
  • Dime por qué. Tell me why.
  • ¿Por qué no vamos al cine? Why don’t we go to the movies? (suggestion)

The accent appears even without question marks, because the meaning is still interrogative.

Porque: because

One word, no accent. It introduces a cause or reason:

  • No fui porque estaba enfermo. I didn’t go because I was ill.
  • —¿Por qué estudias español? —Porque me encanta.
  • Lo hago porque quiero. I do it because I want to.
{{image:2}}

El porqué: the reason

One word, with an accent, and always used as a noun, usually with el or another determiner. It can be plural:

  • Quiero saber el porqué de su decisión. I want to know the reason for his decision.
  • Los porqués de la vida. Life’s whys.

Test: if you can replace it with la razón or el motivo, write porqué.

Por que: the rare one

Two words, no accent. It appears in two cases:

  • Preposition por + relative que, often replaceable by por el cual / la cual: Ese es el motivo por que (por el cual) te llamé.
  • After verbs that take por: Me preocupo por que todo salga bien (I make sure that everything goes well). Optar por que…, apostar por que…

If you are a learner, you can safely avoid this form by using por el cual or por la cual.

{{book:the-mind-lies}}

Why this is tricky, even for natives

All four forms sound almost the same in speech, so the difference is purely visual. Learners face an extra trap: in English, “why” and “because” are completely different words, so learners rarely confuse the meaning, but they often forget the accent or the space. Spanish teachers report that porque in questions is one of the most frequent spelling mistakes among native speakers too. Getting it right is a small signal of careful writing, which matters in emails, job applications and anything published.

A quick mental shortcut

Question, even an indirect one? Two words, accent: por qué. Answer or reason? One word, no accent: porque. With el in front? One word with accent: porqué. Everything else? You probably don’t need it.

Real conversation

  • A: ¿Por qué te vas tan pronto? (Why are you leaving so early?)
  • B: Porque mañana madrugo. (Because I’m getting up early tomorrow.)
  • A: Ya, pero nunca entiendo el porqué de tus horarios. (Sure, but I never understand the reason for your schedule.)

One extra tip for texting: many native speakers write xq or pq for both forms in chats. It is fine with friends, but in anything formal, write the full form correctly.

A related form worth knowing is como at the start of a sentence, which often replaces porque when the reason comes first: Como llovía, no salimos (As it was raining, we didn’t go out).

Common mistakes

IncorrectCorrectWhy
¿Porque no vienes?¿Por qué no vienes?Question: two words, accent
No vine por qué llovía.No vine porque llovía.Reason: one word
No sé porque se fue.No sé por qué se fue.Indirect question
Explícame el por qué.Explícame el porqué.Noun: one word
¿Por que?¿Por qué?Accent on qué
{{image:3}}

Try it yourself

  1. Why are you laughing? (¿Por qué te ríes?)
  2. Because you’re funny. (Porque eres gracioso.)
  3. I don’t know why. (No sé por qué.)
  4. Nobody explained the reason. (Nadie explicó el porqué.)
  5. Why not? (¿Por qué no?)

Question words also matter in {{link:que-vs-cual|qué vs cuál}} and {{link:spanish-accent-marks|Spanish accent marks}}. More pairs in {{link:spanish-confusing-words|my complete list of Spanish confusing words}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Why: por qué. Because: porque. The reason: el porqué. Master those three, keep por que in your passive knowledge, and your written Spanish will look polished.

faq.q: What is the difference between porque and por qué?
faq.a: Por qué (two words, accent) means why and is used in questions. Porque (one word, no accent) means because and introduces a reason.
When it is a noun meaning the reason, usually with an article: el porqué de su decisión.

faq.q: Does por qué need an accent in indirect questions?
faq.a: Yes: No sé por qué se fue. The accent marks the interrogative meaning even without question marks.
